<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

While auditing the NPU test registrations we found that several tests request far more cards than they actually use. For example, `test_npu_pd_disaggregation` only occupies 4 cards (prefill tp2 on cards 0-1, decode tp2 on cards 2-3) but is registered to the 16-card suite, which wastes runner capacity and adds queueing time to the nightly pipeline.

This is a temporary CI-only PR used to verify that the four audited tests can actually run on runners sized to the cards they use. In the first validation run all four passed on 4-, 2- and 8-card runners, so `test_npu_load_balance_method_pd_disaggregation` was additionally adjusted to fit 4 cards. It is not intended to be merged as-is; the temporary registrations and jobs will be reverted once the validation is done.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Add temporary `register_npu_ci(..., suite="tmp-...", nightly=True)` registrations, sized by the cards each test actually uses (all marked with `TEMP` comments):
  - `test_npu_pd_disaggregation.py` -> `tmp-nightly-4-npu-a3`: prefill `--tp-size 2` (cards 0-1) + decode `--tp-size 2` (cards 2-3) = 4 cards.
  - `test_npu_load_balance_method_pd_disaggregation.py` -> `tmp-nightly-4-npu-a3`: 4 cards in total. Its prefill `--base-gpu-id` was changed from 4 to 0, because prefill tp2 on cards 4-5 plus decode tp2 on cards 2-3 required at least 6 visible cards.
  - `test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_2p_in64k_out1k_prefix90_50ms.py` and `test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_w8a8_1p_in64k_out1k_50ms.py` -> `tmp-nightly-perf-2-npu-a3`: both use `--tp-size 2`, i.e. 2 cards.
- `nightly-test-npu.yml`: add the two matching jobs (`tmp-nightly-4-npu-a3`, `tmp-nightly-perf-2-npu-a3`) and set every other job, including `check-all-jobs`, to `if: false`, so a run only exercises the temporary jobs. `set-image-config` stays enabled because the new jobs depend on it.
- No changes to `test/run_suite.py`: NPU is not in `_SUITE_CHECKED_BACKENDS`, so the temporary suite names are collected by name and only trigger the existing "unknown suite" warning.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Not applicable. This PR only touches NPU CI wiring and test registration; no model, kernel or runtime code is changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

Not applicable. No inference path is modified.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
